headline: Samsung Galaxy A38 5G could pack a massive 6000mAh battery
summary: The popular mid-range phone may see a significant battery upgrade from 5000mAh to 6000mAh, potentially extending screen time.
details: Samsung's Galaxy A38 5G is reportedly set to feature a substantial 6000mAh battery, a notable increase from the 5000mAh capacity found in its predecessor, the Galaxy A37. This upgrade could offer users considerably longer battery life.

The device's rated capacity is listed as 5882mAh, which translates to the advertised 6000mAh typical capacity. This larger cell would position the Galaxy A38 more competitively against other mid-range phones that already offer larger batteries.

This isn't the first time Samsung has equipped an A-series phone with a 6000mAh battery; the entry-level Galaxy A07 also features this capacity, delivering substantially longer runtimes. The Galaxy A38 is expected to retain 45W fast charging, which will be important for topping up the larger battery.

While the battery capacity is expected to increase, other specifications like cameras and design are reportedly staying the same, though new color options might be introduced. The phone could also see an upgrade to a faster Exynos processor with improved graphics.
Samsung is anticipated to officially announce the Galaxy A38, alongside the Galaxy A58 and A28, in February or March 2026, aligning with their typical hardware release cycle.

headline: Snap has over 30 million paid subscribers across Snapchat+ and other plans
summary: The company announced this milestone during its Q3 earnings, with non-advertising revenue growing 84% year-over-year, largely due to AI-powered features.
details: Snap announced it has surpassed 30 million paid subscribers across its various subscription plans, including Snapchat+. This milestone was revealed during the company's third-quarter earnings report, highlighting an 84% growth in non-advertising revenue compared to the previous year.

Snapchat+ was launched in 2022, offering bonus features like seeing who re-watched Stories. Since then, Snap has expanded its offerings to include Lens+ for AI-powered AR effects, Platinum for an ad-free experience, and paid storage for Memories.

While a breakdown of subscribers per plan wasn't provided, Lens+ has seen nearly 600% growth since January 2026, suggesting strong user enthusiasm for AI features like AI Photoshoot. CEO Evan Spiegel noted that AI-powered features have exceeded expectations in driving demand for paid products.

This growth in subscriptions is a bright spot for Snap, especially as advertising revenue grew "below ambitions" and daily user growth was modest. For comparison, X reported approximately 6.3 million paid subscribers across its premium offerings earlier this year.

Snap also announced a shift to reporting monthly active users instead of daily users starting in 2027, with Snapchat currently having 977 million monthly users. The company also acknowledged potential impacts from legal challenges and increased regulatory scrutiny regarding youth-related issues.
